text:
Here are three creative ways to transform your leftover salmon, baby potatoes, dill, pasta, and garlic into new, appealing dishes:

1. **Creamy Salmon and Potato Pasta Bake**
   Dice the leftover salmon and halve the baby potatoes. Boil the pasta until al dente. Sauté minced garlic in olive oil, then add the potatoes and cook until tender. Stir in the salmon, cooked pasta, and a generous amount of chopped dill. Mix with a creamy sauce (such as a simple béchamel or a yogurt-based sauce if you have it on hand), top with breadcrumbs, and bake until golden. The dill provides a fresh, herbal note that cuts through the richness of the salmon and cream.

2. **Cold Salmon and Potato Pasta Salad**
   Cook the pasta and let it cool. Boil or roast the baby potatoes until soft, then cool and slice them. Flake the leftover salmon into chunks. Create a vinaigrette using olive oil, lemon juice (if available), minced garlic, and plenty of fresh dill. Toss the cooled pasta, potatoes, and salmon together with the dressing. This dish is refreshing and highlights the natural flavors of the dill and garlic without heavy cooking.

3. **Garlic-Dill Salmon and Potato Skillet with Pasta**
   Sauté minced garlic in butter or oil until fragrant. Add the halved baby potatoes and cook until crispy and golden. Flake in the leftover salmon and gently warm it through, being careful not to overcook. Stir in the cooked pasta and toss everything together. Finish with a heavy sprinkle of fresh dill. This one-pan meal combines the textures of crispy potatoes, tender salmon, and chewy pasta, all bound by the aromatic garlic and dill.
